title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 3rd District

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled after no other Democrat qualified to challenge incumbent Morgan McGarvey; he advanced automatically.

candidates.name: Morgan McGarvey
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without opposition after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Morgan McGarvey is the Democratic incumbent for Kentucky's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A Louisville attorney, he served in the Kentucky State Senate from 2012 to 2023, including as Senate Democratic Caucus minority leader. According to his official site, he emphasizes public education, organized labor, reproductive rights and working families.

background.text: Born in Louisville, Kentucky, in 1979, according to Ballotpedia; his official biography calls him a lifelong Louisvillian who graduated from Manual High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Missouri in 2002 and a law degree from the University of Kentucky in 2007.
Worked as an attorney with Morgan & Pottinger PSC, according to Ballotpedia.
Has been affiliated with the Young Professionals Association of Louisville and the New Leaders Council, according to Ballotpedia.
Served in the Kentucky State Senate, District 19, from 2012 to 2023, including four years as Minority Leader of the Senate Democratic Caucus.

His official biography says he wrote and passed 18 bills into law during roughly ten years in the State Senate, including an insurance mandate for low-birthweight infants and a law letting Simmons College of Kentucky lower tuition.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2022. Serves on the Veterans' Affairs, Small Business and Budget committees and co-chairs the Bourbon Caucus and the Ohio River Basin Caucus, according to his official site.
His official site says he was the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill out of the House, a bill on veterans' educational benefits.
According to his official biography, he lives in the Highlands neighborhood of Louisville with his wife, Chris, and their three children.

priorities.text: Describes his work in Congress as fighting for public education, organized labor, and reproductive rights, and for Kentucky's working families.

positions.summary: Co-sponsored H.R. 715 (Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2023) and H.R. 698 (Assault Weapons Ban of 2023), and lists work to pass gun legislation as a top priority on his official issues page.

Released a statement supporting Planned Parenthood's lawsuit to restore abortion rights in Kentucky, describing the state's abortion ban as having created "second-class citizenship" and calling to "restore equal rights under the law."
positions.quote: Since the fall of Roe, Kentucky's draconian abortion ban has created second-class citizenship for half our commonwealth and caused undue suffering for women in need. It is beyond time to restore equal rights under the law.

positions.summary: Opposed additional ICE funding in a House floor speech and voted no on the bill adding $70 billion for ICE and CBP, saying he would not give ICE “another dollar.”
positions.quote: We shouldn’t give them another dollar.

positions.summary: In a House floor speech opposing additional ICE funding, said the money could instead bring back the health care tax credits that expired.
positions.quote: We could bring back the healthcare tax credits that Republicans killed because “too expensive” for three more years.

positions.summary: Said the decision to go to war rests with Congress and voted for a war powers resolution on Iran, stating Congress never authorized the war.
positions.quote: The grave responsibility of putting our servicemembers in harm’s way, plus spending the billions of taxpayer dollars this war will cost, rests squarely with Congress and the people who send them there.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittees on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs, and Economic Opportunity) and the House Committee on Small Business, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development (118th Congress, 2023-2024).
Co-sponsored H.R. 715, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2023, and H.R. 698, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2023.

candidates.name: Maria Teresa Rodriguez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 48.2% of the vote, defeating David Nichter, Daniel Cobble and Donald Pay.

summary.text: Maria Teresa Rodriguez is the Republican nominee for Kentucky's 3rd Congressional District. Her campaign describes her as having lived through political persecution before coming to the United States, and its site lists safe streets, a strong economy, lower taxes, legal immigration, protecting the unborn and protecting women's sports as priorities.

background.text: According to her campaign website, her path went "from political persecution to public service" and she is running to defend freedoms she once lived without.
Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for Kentucky's 3rd District, defeating David Nichter, Daniel Cobble and Donald Pay.

priorities.text: "María is running for Congress to defend the freedoms she once lived without. She believes strongly in free enterprise, safe communities, legal immigration, and protecting the constitutional rights of all Americans."
